paragraphs: An inline pump sits in the pipe rather than beside it, which saves a foundation and a great deal of floor. Vertical mounting puts the motor above the wet end, so a seal failure drips onto the floor instead of into the windings.
The model holds 63,299 polygons and 63,440 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, in red, and carries StemCell certification.
At $29 it suits building services and industrial visualisation, plant room scenes, equipment marketing, technical documentation, training material and game environments. On sale since 2026.

Narrow gauge existed because it was cheap. Tighter curves, lighter rail and smaller earthworks meant a line could be pushed into a quarry, a mine or a forest for a fraction of the cost, and almost all of them were built to serve one industry.
The model is light at 32,578 polygons and 33,911 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $29 it suits industrial and heritage visualisation, mine and quarry scenes, railway presentation, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Isopropyl alcohol is the solvent that cleans electronics because it evaporates completely and leaves nothing behind. The spray bottle is the least interesting part and the reason the chemical is in every workshop drawer.
The model is light at 39,755 polygons and 39,730 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $29 it suits product and packaging visualisation, workshop and laboratory scenes, e-commerce and retail imagery, technical material, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Retro styled speakers are selling a memory of hifi rather than hifi itself. The quilted grille and the metal trim reference a specific era, and the electronics behind them are entirely modern with a streaming service inside.
The model is supplied in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and is built to CheckMate specification.
At $29 it suits product and audio visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, interior and lifestyle scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The square bottle and the slanted label were both introduced to solve shipping problems, and they became the most recognisable pair of design decisions in the spirits trade. Square bottles do not roll and pack without wasted space.
The model is light at 10,760 polygons and 10,634 vertices in polygonal geometry with overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $29 it suits beverage and packaging visualisation, label mockups, e-commerce and retail imagery, bar and interior scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The kettle grill is a lid and two vents, and that is the entire innovation. Controlling airflow at the bottom and the top turns an open fire into an oven, which is why this shape took over barbecuing almost completely.
The model holds 348,372 polygons and 175,699 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits garden and outdoor visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, terrace and lifestyle scenes, film props and game environments. On sale since 2024.

A key cabinet is an admission that a building has more locks than anybody can carry. Numbered hooks, a written log and one key that opens the cabinet itself: the whole system depends on that last key being managed properly.
The model holds 323,298 polygons and 164,021 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits facilities and security visualisation, office and interior scenes, equipment marketing, e-commerce imagery, film props and game environments. On sale since 2022.

Oven gloves are a heat problem disguised as textiles. The insulation has to be thick enough to hold a hot tray and thin enough to feel it, and every design is a compromise between burning a hand and dropping the dish.
The model is extremely light at 3,736 polygons and 3,752 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits kitchen and interior visualisation, product and e-commerce imagery, advertising, cooking scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

The knife rest is a portable barricade that can be dragged across a road in seconds and dragged back again. That is its entire advantage over anything dug in, and it is why the same design has been used at checkpoints for a century.
The model holds 94,788 polygons and 93,505 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits military and security visualisation, checkpoint and border scenes, documentary graphics, film and television sets, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

The cup carrier is a piece of packaging that exists entirely because hands run out. It is moulded pulp, it is thrown away in under ten minutes, and it solves a problem that had defeated cafes for decades.
The model is very light at 16,532 polygons and 8,264 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the holder with three cups. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits food and beverage visualisation, packaging and branding mockups, e-commerce imagery, cafe and street scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

A plaque buckle is a flat panel rather than a frame, which means the belt threads through and lies smooth under a shirt. It is the buckle chosen when the wearer wants the belt to be visible but not to catch on anything.
The model is light at 20,792 polygons and 10,426 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $29 it suits apparel and accessory visualisation, e-commerce and catalogue imagery, character wardrobe work, advertising, film costume and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

A sky lantern is a hot air balloon with a candle in it, and that is exactly the problem: it lands still burning, wherever the wind takes it. Several countries have banned them for that reason, and they remain a fixture of festival imagery.
The model is very light at 10,312 polygons and 10,278 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, in white. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $29 it suits festival and event visualisation, night and celebration scenes, advertising, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The plastic cased mine was designed to defeat metal detectors, and the consequence has outlived every conflict it was laid in. Clearance teams still deal with these decades later, which is why demining imagery matters as much as military imagery.

The model is light at 19,668 polygons and 19,157 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in aged condition, textured with 5 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries StemCell certification, and a second build is offered separately.
At $29 it suits demining and humanitarian visualisation, documentary and news graphics, defence presentation, training material, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

A sea pen is a floating collar with a net hanging beneath it, and the collar is doing almost all the engineering. It has to stay circular in swell, support people walking on it, and hold a volume of water containing several hundred tonnes of fish.

The model holds 42,155 polygons and 43,377 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification, and larger builds with access bridge and buoys are offered separately.
At $29 it suits aquaculture and marine visualisation, food industry presentation, coastal and offshore scenes, documentary graphics, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.
